SK8020 A class with [TestMethod] members carries no [TestClass]

A class declares MSTest [TestMethod] members and is not itself marked [TestClass], so MSTest discovers none of them and the suite is green because nothing ran.

CategoryTests
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, review it
Language version floor—
Since1.3

Why

This is the worst failure a test can have, because it does not look like a failure. MSTest's discoverer enumerates types carrying [TestClass] and only then looks at their methods; a class without the attribute is never opened, so every [TestMethod] in it is silently skipped. Nothing is reported as ignored, no runner prints a warning, and the count of executed tests simply does not include them — a suite that was never run and a suite that passed are the same colour. The signal is decidable from attributes alone, which is what separates it from SK8001: no call has to be followed and no assertion has to be recognised, so there is no undecidable middle for the rule to guess at.

Example

Instead of:

using Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.UnitTesting;

public sealed class ArchetypeTests {
    [TestMethod]
    public void Counts() {
        Assert.AreEqual(1, 1);
    }
}

Write:

using Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.UnitTesting;

[TestClass]
public sealed class ArchetypeTests {
    [TestMethod]
    public void Counts() {
        Assert.AreEqual(1, 1);
    }
}

When it does not fire

⚠ MSTest only, deliberately, and the other two frameworks are silence rather than coverage. xUnit discovers a [Fact] in any public class and has no class-level attribute to be missing; NUnit has made [TestFixture] optional since NUnit 3 for a non-generic, non-parameterised class, so its absence is not a defect. A rule that fired on those would be reporting a convention, not a bug. The whole analyzer withdraws unless Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.UnitTesting.TestMethodAttribute resolves in the compilation, so a repository with no MSTest reference never sees it. ⚠ The attribute is matched by symbol through its base chain, never by written name, so [DataTestMethod] and a repository's own [TestMethod]-derived attribute are both recognised and somebody else's type called TestMethodAttribute is not. ⚠ [TestClass] is looked for on the symbol and on every base type, so a partial class carrying it in another file and a base class carrying it for its derived fixtures are both silence. ⚠ `abstract` and `static` classes never fire. An abstract class holding [TestMethod] members is the shared-base pattern MSTest supports — the attribute belongs on the concrete class that inherits them — and a static class cannot be a test class at all. ⚠ One finding per type, not per partial part, anchored at the first declaring reference in file order, because two findings would each carry an insertion of an attribute that AllowMultiple forbids twice. ⚠ The other direction the upstream idea pairs with this one is not implemented and that is a decision, not an omission. "A public method in a [TestClass] has no test attribute" is not decidable from attributes: a public helper, a public fixture property, a public constructor and a [TestInitialize] spelled through somebody's own attribute are all legitimate, and the rule would fire on the ordinary shape of every test file. ⚠ `fixIsSafe` is false, and not because the edit is uncertain. There is exactly one repair and it is one token. Its effect is that tests which have never executed begin executing, and the first run after it is applied may be red — which is the rule finishing its sentence and is still a thing a person reads before pushing.
